newsitem.title: UK: South Brazil focus of interest in sugar freight mkt.
newsitem.headline: South Brazil focus of interest in sugar freight mkt.

text.p: New orders from south Brazil dominated activity on London's sugar freight market on Tuesday as the ports of Santos and Paranagua geared up for this season's cycle of sugar shipments.
Cargill returned to the market with another freight order out of south Brazil as part of its hefty physical delivery against New York's May futures contract.
It quoted for 14,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Santos or Paranagua to Algeria, Egyptian Med, Black Sea or Baltic for prompt to May 23 dates.
Shipbrokers said Cargill was also open for 14,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Puerto Quetzal to Valparaiso.
South Brazil also featured in another two orders.
Glencore quoted for 14,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Santos or Paranagua to Pakistan for June 1/5, although shipbrokers said the specified shipment dates appeared to be quite narrow.
E D & F Man was in the market for a bagged 13,750-tonne cargo from south Brazil to Chittagong for prompt dates and 15,000 tonnes in bulk from Paranagua to the Philippines for May/June.
Pacol was said to have fixed 14,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Cuba to the Black Sea for prompt shipments. Details of the rate achieved have yet to emerge.
Shipbrokers said a tweendecker cargo had been fixed out of Maputo for about 14,000 tonnes but there were no more details immediately available.

Elsewhere, officials at Russia's Black Sea port of Novorossiisk said around 90,000 tonnes of raw sugar, mostly if not all of Cuban origin, was held up at the port and would take about one month to clear.
The raws backlog was around 140,000 tonnes, just under a month ago, mainly due to bad weather and the lack of railway wagons to take sugar to refineries.
No Brazilian raws have yet been reported at the port, the official said.
In Brazil, the CODESP port authority at Santos has deposited outstanding April salaries, removing any need for further industrial action.
